senses.gloss: m.(b. h. עֹל; עָלַל)yoke; also pole of a wagon.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Kilayim 2:6">Kil. II, 6</cite> <he>מלא הע׳ השרוני</he> the width of the yoke (the team) used in the plain of Sharon.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 14:4">Kel. XIV, 4</cite> <he>הע׳ של מתכות</he> a metal pole (v. Maim. a. l.); ib. 5 <he>הע׳ המצופה</he> the metal-tipped pole.
<cite ref="Sifrei Bamidbar 123:1">Sifré Num. 123</cite> <he>בע׳ שלא לעבודה וכ׳</he> the text speaks of a yoke not put on for working.
Sot. 46ᵃ ע׳ פוסל בין בשעת וכ׳ the bearing of a yoke disqualifies the animal for the ceremony, whether it was put on at working time &c.; a. fr.—Trnsf. obligation, dependence.

<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 3:5">Ab. III, 5</cite> <he>כל המקבל עליו ע׳ תורה … ע׳ מלכות וע׳ דרך ארץ</he> whosoever takes upon himself the yoke (obligations) of the Law, from him shall be removed the yoke of government (oppression) and the yoke of worldly affairs; <he>וכל הפורק ממנו ע׳ תורה וכ׳</he> but he who throws off the yoke of the Law, will be made to feel the yoke of &c.

<cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 2:2">Ber. II, 2</cite> <he>כדי שיקבל עליו ע׳ מלכות שמים … ע׳ מצות</he> in order that he may acknowledge his dependence on divine government first (by reciting <cite ref="Deuteronomy 6:4">Deut. VI, 4</cite> sq., v. <cite ref="U01512"><he>שְׁמַע</he></cite>) and then his subjection to religious duties (by reciting <cite ref="Deuteronomy 11:13">Deut. XI, 13</cite> sq.); a. fr.—Pl.) <he>עוּלִּין</he>. Tanḥ. V’zoth 5 <he>שני ע׳ וכ׳</he> thou puttest two yokes upon thy children; Yalk. Deut. 952.
